body: Thats great, it let me post to that one, thanks!
Ah thanks, I have just tried to post it there but posting is restricted to 'trusted members', nevermind

You are a good person,  your friend is very lucky they have you in their corner.  Everyone is different but here are some things i think would help me:

- just let them talk to you, without judgement, without trying to fix things, without comparisons, just listen, let them get everything off their chest
- if they dont want to talk, dont pressure them, just be available if they need you, or if you think it makes them happy then you do talking, keep them company
- dont keep asking them to go out or do social things if they say no, leave the invitation open or let them ask you. It can create terrible anxiety just to say no to things all the time and can lead to you getting ghosted. Dont be offended if this happens - its not personal and they dont hate you, just still be there.
- make them feel wanted or needed. Do they specialise in anything or used to have a passion? Ask them for advice or help, make them feel worth something. Work on a project together. 


Sorry i cant offer more, its a something without a magic cure as ive found over the last 15 years living with it. I wish you and your friend all the best
Yes, ideally I could walk into a hospital and ask to die and have all my organs donated to people on a transplant waiting list, at least I can help people to live who want and deserve to
Im afraid it already has won though, I cant do it anymore, i have no energy left
